objects.definition: #define RTENTRY struct rtentry
objects.description: Macro alias mapping RTENTRY to the system routing table entry structure type struct rtentry. This header does not define struct rtentry itself; it only creates an alias macro. The actual struct is provided by system headers (e.g., <net/route.h>).

objects.definition: #define NETSNMP_SELECT_TIMEVAL struct timeval
objects.description: Macro alias mapping NETSNMP_SELECT_TIMEVAL to struct timeval, used to describe the type of the fifth argument to select(). The underlying struct timeval is defined by system headers (<sys/time.h>).

objects.definition: #define NETSNMP_FD_MASK_TYPE __fd_mask
objects.description: Macro alias mapping NETSNMP_FD_MASK_TYPE to the platform fd_set bitmask element type (__fd_mask). The actual __fd_mask type is provided by system headers (typically <sys/select.h>).

objects.definition: #define NETSNMP_SELECT_TIMEVAL struct timeval
objects.description: Alias tying NETSNMP_SELECT_TIMEVAL to struct timeval. Provided here for completeness with pointer canonicalization. The real struct timeval is defined in system headers.

objects.definition:
#if defined(WIN32) && !defined(cygwin)
typedef HANDLE netsnmp_pid_t;
#define NETSNMP_NO_SUCH_PROCESS INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE
#else
/*
 * Note: on POSIX-compliant systems, pid_t is defined in <sys/types.h>.
 * And if pid_t has not been defined in <sys/types.h>, AC_TYPE_PID_T ensures
 * that a pid_t definition is present in net-snmp-config.h.
 */
typedef pid_t netsnmp_pid_t;
#define NETSNMP_NO_SUCH_PROCESS -1
#endif
objects.description: Typedef alias for a process identifier used by Net-SNMP. Maps to HANDLE on Windows or pid_t on POSIX. Use NETSNMP_NO_SUCH_PROCESS as an invalid sentinel. Construction is by assignment from system APIs; no destructor.

objects.definition:
#ifndef HAVE_SOCKLEN_T
#ifdef WIN32
typedef int socklen_t;
#else
typedef u_int socklen_t;
#endif
#endif
objects.description: Typedef for socket length type when the platform lacks socklen_t. Matches int on Windows, u_int otherwise. Provided for portability.

objects.definition:
#ifndef HAVE_SSIZE_T
#if defined(__INT_MAX__) && __INT_MAX__ == 2147483647
typedef int ssize_t;
#else
typedef long ssize_t;
#endif
#endif
objects.description: Fallback typedef for signed size type when not provided by the system headers. Either int or long depending on platform configuration.
Lightweight wrapper struct holding an opaque pointer to a PCRE regex object. Defined only when PCRE is available. The regex_ptr points to an underlying PCRE structure managed elsewhere.

Union of pointers to various SNMP value representations used in variable bindings (integers, strings, OIDs, bitstrings, 64-bit counters, and optionally floats/doubles). The union holds pointers; memory ownership is external to this union.

Linked-list node representing an SNMP variable binding: OID name, type, value (via netsnmp_vardata), and auxiliary storage/hooks. next_variable chains the list. Caller manages memory for name/value; dataFreeHook can clean data.

Primary SNMP Protocol Data Unit structure encompassing version-independent fields, v1/v2c community and trap data, v3 security/context fields, transport metadata, and a linked list of variable bindings (variables). Memory management follows Net-SNMP APIs; ensure to free variables and allocated strings appropriately.

Session configuration and state for SNMP operations: transport endpoints, callbacks, security parameters (v1/v2c/v3), message size limits, and auxiliary pointers. Created/managed by Net-SNMP session APIs; fields are typically set via helper functions or initialization macros.

objects.definition:
typedef int        (*snmp_callback) (int, netsnmp_session *, int,
                                          netsnmp_pdu *, void *);
objects.description: Function pointer type for SNMP library callbacks invoked with operation code, session pointer, request id, PDU pointer, and user data. Return int status.

objects.definition:
typedef int     (*netsnmp_callback) (int, netsnmp_session *, int,
                                          netsnmp_pdu *, void *);
objects.description: Alias typedef for a function pointer matching snmp_callback signature. Used generically within Net-SNMP APIs.
Statistics for traps/informs sent and acknowledged, including counts and last event times (in sysUpTime ticks). Present only when trap stats are enabled.
Simple container for an index comprised of an OID array with length. Often used for table indexing in SNMP MIB helpers. Caller manages memory for oids.
Generic dynamically-sized array of void* with a recorded element count. Caller manages allocation and element lifetime.
Single-pointer wrapper to allow pass-by-reference semantics for a void* value in APIs.
Convenience union able to hold various common C scalar types and pointers, used for generic value passing/storing.

Enhanced fd_set-like structure capable of handling large file descriptor sets. Must be initialized with netsnmp_large_fd_set_init() and cleaned with netsnmp_large_fd_set_cleanup() to avoid leaks. lfs_setptr points to internal or dynamically allocated storage depending on set size.

objects.definition: struct session_list;
objects.description: Opaque forward declaration for the library’s per-session handle used by the single-session API (snmp_sess_*). The actual structure is not defined in this header, making it an incomplete type intended to be used as an opaque handle/pointer by callers.

objects.definition: struct timeval;
objects.description: Forward declaration of the POSIX timeval structure, used here only as a referenced type for timeouts. The full definition is not provided in this header.

Opaque handle to an SNMP Protocol Data Unit (PDU) object used by Net-SNMP. The concrete struct/type is not defined in this header; it is only referenced here via function declarations and is defined elsewhere (likely in included Net-SNMP headers).

Opaque variable-binding node type used by Net-SNMP to represent a single varbind (and to form varbind lists). This header only references the type; its full definition is not provided here and is expected from included Net-SNMP headers (e.g., <net-snmp/types.h>).
Opaque SNMP PDU handle used by Net-SNMP. This header references it for adding variables to a PDU but does not define it here.
Alias type for an OID component array element used throughout Net-SNMP to represent object identifiers. Only referenced here; actual typedef is defined elsewhere.
C standard I/O stream pointer. Referenced for printing functions; defined by the C standard library, not in this header.
Opaque MIB tree node type used by Net-SNMP for representing parsed MIB modules. Only forward-referenced here; its full definition is in another header (likely <net-snmp/library/mib.h>).

objects.definition: struct session_list;
objects.description: Forward declaration of an internal session list structure used by Net-SNMP for session management. The actual structure layout is not defined in this header.

objects.definition: struct variable_list;
objects.description: Forward declaration of a structure representing a list of SNMP variables (varbinds). The full definition is not provided in this header.

functions.name: netsnmp_bigendian
functions.description: Returns a nonzero value if the host byte order is big-endian, and zero if little-endian. Implemented as a small inline helper using a union to examine the first byte of an unsigned long. Intended to be used when compile-time endianness macros are unavailable; when __BYTE_ORDER__ is defined, NETSNMP_BIGENDIAN is a macro instead. Note: in this header the function is declared with NETSNMP_STATIC_INLINE, which typically expands to "static inline" unless inlining is disabled.
requirements: No arguments; may be called at any time.
Header must be included so the static inline definition is visible; the function has internal linkage (do not expect external linkage).
Return is 0 (little-endian) or nonzero (big-endian). Behavior for non-standard mixed-endian architectures is not defined by this helper.

functions.name: snmp_sess_init
functions.description: Initialize a netsnmp_session structure with library defaults. Typically called before filling in session fields and calling snmp_open/snmmp_sess_open.
requirements: session must be a valid, writable pointer to a netsnmp_session structure
Call before using the session with snmp_open or snmp_sess_open

functions.name: snmp_open
functions.description: Create and open an SNMP session using the parameters in the provided netsnmp_session. Opens/binds necessary transport (e.g., UDP). Returns a session handle (different from the input pointer) or NULL on error (snmp_errno set).
requirements: session must point to an initialized netsnmp_session (typically via snmp_sess_init) with required fields configured
Caller must check for NULL return and consult snmp_errno on error
Do not assume the returned handle equals the input pointer; store and use the returned netsnmp_session* for subsequent operations

functions.name: snmp_close
functions.description: Close a single SNMP session, freeing all allocated session data, dequeuing pending requests, and closing sockets. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: session must be a valid, open session previously returned by snmp_open
Caller should check the return value: 1 indicates success, 0 indicates error

functions.name: snmp_close_sessions
functions.description: Close all open SNMP sessions, freeing associated resources and closing sockets. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: Should be called when no further SNMP operations are required across any open sessions
Caller should check the return value for success (1) or error (0)

functions.name: _build_initial_pdu_packet
functions.description: Internal helper to build the initial wire packet for a PDU on a specific session, with optional bulk behavior. Details are not documented in this header.
requirements: slp must be a valid pointer to a session_list associated with an open session
pdu must be a valid, initialized netsnmp_pdu
bulk is an integer flag (nonzero likely enables bulk-related encoding); exact accepted values are not documented

functions.name: snmp_send
functions.description: Serialize and send a PDU on a session. Sets PDU defaults from the session if needed, tracks the outstanding request, and transmits the PDU. Returns the request ID if applicable (or 1 in a special case when the request ID is 0); returns 0 on error. The PDU is freed by snmp_send unless a failure occurred.
requirements: session must be a valid, open session returned by snmp_open
pdu must point to a valid, heap-allocated netsnmp_pdu appropriate for the request
Caller must not free or reuse pdu after a successful send (it is freed by the library)
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates error; a positive value is the request ID or 1 if the request ID is 0

functions.name: snmp_async_send
functions.signature: int snmp_async_send(netsnmp_session *session, netsnmp_pdu *pdu, netsnmp_callback callback, void *cb_data);
functions.description: Asynchronously serialize and send a PDU. Stores the callback and user data with the outstanding request, then transmits. Returns the request ID if applicable (otherwise 1); returns 0 on error. The PDU is freed by the library unless a failure occurred.
requirements: session must be a valid, open session returned by snmp_open
pdu must point to a valid, heap-allocated netsnmp_pdu
callback must be a valid function conforming to netsnmp_callback and must be prepared to handle response or timeout notifications
Caller must not free or reuse pdu after a successful send
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates error

functions.name: snmp_read
functions.description: Process readable SNMP sockets indicated in fdset: read packets, parse them, and dispatch resulting PDUs to their session callbacks. Successfully handled PDUs and corresponding requests are deleted.
requirements: fdset must be initialized by the caller, typically by first calling snmp_select_info to OR SNMP fds into the set and then running select
Only fds that are set in fdset will be processed

functions.name: snmp_read2
functions.description: Like snmp_read(), but accepts a netsnmp_large_fd_set instead of a regular fd_set to support large fd indexes.
requirements: fdset must be a valid, initialized netsnmp_large_fd_set containing SNMP fds set by snmp_select_info2 or similar
Only fds that are set in fdset will be processed

functions.name: snmp_synch_response
functions.description: Synchronous helper: send a PDU on the given session and wait for a response, returning the response PDU via output parameter. Not documented here; behavior inferred from name and common Net-SNMP usage.
requirements: session must be a valid, open session
pdu must be a valid netsnmp_pdu for the request
response must be a non-NULL pointer to receive an allocated netsnmp_pdu*; caller is typically responsible for freeing the response PDU
Caller should check the integer return code to determine success or failure (exact values not documented here)

functions.name: snmp_select_info
functions.signature: int snmp_select_info(int *numfds, fd_set *fdset, struct timeval *timeout, int *block);
functions.description: Provide parameters for a select() call that services all SNMP sessions: OR SNMP sockets into fdset, compute the earliest timeout for SNMP activity, and indicate whether select should block. Returns the number of open sockets (i.e., number of open sessions).
requirements: numfds must be a valid pointer; on return contains the number of significant fds
fdset must be a valid pointer to an fd_set that can be modified (SNMP fds are OR’d into it)

timeout must be a valid pointer to a struct timeval; when block is input as 1, its incoming value is ignored but it must be available for the function to set; on return, if block is true, timeout’s value is undefined
block must be a valid pointer to an int; input 1 requests blocking indefinitely; output indicates whether select should block indefinitely
Caller should call snmp_read if select reports activity on any SNMP fd, and call snmp_timeout when the computed timeout expires

functions.name: snmp_select_info2
functions.signature: int snmp_select_info2(int *numfds, netsnmp_large_fd_set *fdset, struct timeval *timeout, int *block);
functions.description: Like snmp_select_info(), but operates on a netsnmp_large_fd_set to support large file descriptor values. Returns the number of open sockets.
requirements: numfds must be a valid pointer for input/output
fdset must be a valid pointer to a netsnmp_large_fd_set that can be modified to include SNMP fds
timeout and block have the same semantics and requirements as in snmp_select_info

functions.name: snmp_sess_select_info_flags
functions.signature: int snmp_sess_select_info_flags(struct session_list *slp, int *numfds, fd_set *fdset, struct timeval *timeout, int *block, int flags);
functions.description: Single-session variant of select() parameter preparation with additional flags. Populates fdset and timeout for the specified session. Details of flags are not documented here.
requirements: slp must be a valid pointer obtained from snmp_sess_open
numfds, fdset, timeout, and block must be valid pointers as in snmp_select_info
flags is an integer bitmask; defined values include NETSNMP_SELECT_NOFLAGS and NETSNMP_SELECT_NOALARMS; other effects are not documented here

functions.name: snmp_sess_select_info2_flags
functions.signature: int snmp_sess_select_info2_flags(struct session_list *slp, int *numfds, netsnmp_large_fd_set *fdset, struct timeval *timeout, int *block, int flags);
functions.description: Like snmp_sess_select_info_flags(), but uses netsnmp_large_fd_set to support large file descriptor values.
requirements: slp must be a valid pointer obtained from snmp_sess_open
numfds, fdset, timeout, and block must be valid pointers; semantics mirror snmp_select_info2
flags is an integer bitmask; defined values include NETSNMP_SELECT_NOFLAGS and NETSNMP_SELECT_NOALARMS

functions.name: snmp_timeout
functions.description: Process SNMP timeouts: for any outstanding requests that have expired, retry if retries remain or notify the session callback of timeout. Intended to be called when the select() timeout computed by snmp_select_info expires; function is idempotent and may be polled.
requirements: Should be called whenever the timeout obtained from snmp_select_info expires
May be called repeatedly (idempotent), but polling can be CPU-expensive

functions.name: snmp_sess_open
functions.description: Create and open a single-session context based on the provided netsnmp_session. Returns an opaque session handle (struct session_list*) to be used with snmp_sess_* APIs.
requirements: session must be initialized with snmp_sess_init and configured before calling
Caller must store and use the returned opaque handle for subsequent snmp_sess_* calls
On failure, the function may return NULL (not explicitly stated here); caller should check for NULL

functions.name: snmp_sess_pointer
functions.description: Retrieve a session_list handle associated with a given netsnmp_session. Not documented here; behavior inferred from name.
requirements: session should refer to an existing/open session
Return value semantics (NULL on failure) are not documented; caller should handle a NULL result

functions.name: snmp_sess_session
functions.description: Return a pointer to a netsnmp_session associated with a single-session handle created by snmp_sess_open. The returned netsnmp_session pointer is opaque; do not free it.
requirements: Invoke snmp_sess_session only after a successful snmp_sess_open
sessp must be a valid handle previously returned by snmp_sess_open
Do not free memory returned by snmp_sess_session (per notes)
If the returned value is NULL, treat as failure and abort use as shown in the example

functions.name: snmp_sess_session_lookup
functions.description: Look up and return the netsnmp_session for a given single-session handle. Not documented beyond the name; appears similar to snmp_sess_session.
requirements: sessp must be a valid session handle
Returned pointer should be treated as opaque and not freed
Caller should handle a possible NULL return

functions.name: snmp_sess_lookup_by_name
functions.description: Look up an SNMP session by name/key parameter. Not documented in this header; behavior is inferred from the function name.
requirements: paramName must be a valid, null-terminated string
Caller should handle a NULL return if no session matches or on error

functions.name: snmp_sess_send
functions.description: Single-session variant of snmp_send: serialize and send a PDU for the specified session handle. Returns the request ID if applicable (otherwise 1); returns 0 on error. The PDU is freed by the library unless a failure occurred.
requirements: sessp must be a valid handle from snmp_sess_open
pdu must point to a valid, heap-allocated netsnmp_pdu
Do not free or reuse pdu after a successful send
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates error

functions.name: snmp_sess_async_send
functions.signature: int snmp_sess_async_send(struct session_list *sessp, netsnmp_pdu *pdu, netsnmp_callback callback, void *cb_data);
functions.description: Single-session variant of snmp_async_send: send a PDU asynchronously with a callback and user data. Returns the request ID if applicable (otherwise 1); returns 0 on error. The PDU is freed by the library unless a failure occurred.
requirements: sessp must be a valid handle from snmp_sess_open
pdu must be a valid, heap-allocated netsnmp_pdu
callback must be a valid netsnmp_callback function pointer
Do not free or reuse pdu after a successful send
Caller must check the return value and handle 0 as error

functions.name: snmp_sess_select_info
functions.signature: int snmp_sess_select_info(struct session_list *sessp, int *numfds, fd_set *fdset, struct timeval *timeout, int *block);
functions.description: Prepare select() parameters for a single session: OR the session’s sockets into fdset, compute timeout, and indicate blocking behavior. Returns the count contribution for this session.
requirements: sessp must be a valid session handle from snmp_sess_open
numfds, fdset, timeout, and block must be valid pointers; semantics mirror snmp_select_info for a single session

functions.name: snmp_sess_select_info2
functions.signature: int snmp_sess_select_info2(struct session_list *sessp, int *numfds, netsnmp_large_fd_set *fdset, struct timeval *timeout, int *block);
functions.description: Like snmp_sess_select_info(), but operates on a netsnmp_large_fd_set for large fd support.
requirements: sessp must be a valid session handle
numfds, fdset, timeout, and block must be valid pointers; semantics mirror snmp_select_info2 for a single session

functions.name: snmp_sess_read
functions.description: Process readable sockets for a single session using the provided fd_set. Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.
requirements: sessp must be a valid session handle from snmp_sess_open
fdset must be initialized to indicate which descriptors are readable for this session
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success, -1 indicates failure

functions.name: snmp_sess_read2
functions.description: Like snmp_sess_read(), but accepts a netsnmp_large_fd_set for large descriptor values.
requirements: sessp must be a valid session handle
fdset must be a valid, initialized netsnmp_large_fd_set indicating readable descriptors for this session
Caller must check the return value for success (0) or failure (-1)

functions.name: snmp_sess_timeout
functions.description: Handle timeouts for a single session: retry or notify callback when requests expire. Intended to be called when the per-session timeout expires.
requirements: sessp must be a valid session handle
Should be called when the session’s computed timeout expires; may be called idempotently

functions.name: snmp_sess_close
functions.description: Close a single-session handle, freeing resources and closing sockets. Returns an int status (not further documented here).
requirements: slp must be a valid session handle previously returned by snmp_sess_open
Caller should check the return value to determine success or failure

functions.name: snmp_sess_synch_response
functions.description: Synchronous single-session request: send a PDU on the given session handle and wait for the response, returning it via the response pointer. See also snmp_sess_synch_response in snmp_client.h.
requirements: sessp must be a valid session handle from snmp_sess_open
pdu must be a valid netsnmp_pdu for the request
response must be a non-NULL pointer to receive an allocated response PDU; caller is typically responsible for freeing it
Caller should check the integer return code to determine success/failure (exact conventions not documented here)

functions.name: snmp_pdu_create
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new SNMP PDU object for the specified PDU type. Typically used to construct requests (e.g., GET, GETNEXT, SET) or notifications before populating variable bindings and sending via the Net-SNMP session APIs. Details of supported type values are defined by the Net-SNMP PDU/message type constants (e.g., SNMP_MSG_...). If allocation fails, the function is expected to return NULL (inferred).
requirements: type should be a valid Net-SNMP PDU/message type constant as defined in the Net-SNMP headers (e.g., snmp_api.h/asn1.h).
On success, the returned netsnmp_pdu* must be freed with snmp_free_pdu when no longer needed.
Caller must initialize any required PDU fields (e.g., version, community/security params, variable bindings) before use; exact fields depend on intended operation (inferred).
Do not pass an invalid or out-of-range type; behavior is unspecified.

functions.name: snmp_clone_pdu
functions.description: Creates a deep copy of an existing SNMP PDU, returning a new netsnmp_pdu instance that mirrors the input. Useful for retry logic, parallel dispatch, or preserving an original PDU while making modifications. Returns NULL on failure (inferred).
requirements: pdu must be a valid, initialized netsnmp_pdu pointer obtained from Net-SNMP (e.g., snmp_pdu_create or received from the library).
The returned clone must be freed with snmp_free_pdu.
Do not pass NULL unless the implementation explicitly documents NULL-safety; behavior on NULL is unspecified (inferred).
Cloned PDUs may share no ownership of buffers with the original; treat them as independent objects after cloning (inferred).

functions.name: snmp_fix_pdu
functions.description: Adjusts or normalizes an SNMP PDU structure prior to use. Common library patterns suggest it may reconcile fields, indexes, or encoding details so the PDU is consistent for transmission or processing. The idx parameter likely refers to a variable-binding index or error index, but exact semantics are not documented in this header and remain unknown.
requirements: pdu must be a valid netsnmp_pdu pointer created or obtained from Net-SNMP.
idx should be a non-negative integer; the precise acceptable range and meaning are unknown based on this header alone.
Caller should treat the returned netsnmp_pdu* as the (possibly modified) PDU to continue using; if allocation or reallocation occurs internally, the original pointer must not be reused (inferred).
Error handling and return-on-failure behavior are not documented here; callers should be prepared for a NULL return (inferred).

functions.name: snmp_free_pdu
functions.description: Frees a netsnmp_pdu object and all resources owned by it. Use to release PDUs created by snmp_pdu_create, snmp_clone_pdu, or returned by other Net-SNMP APIs. After this call, the pointer must not be used.
requirements: pdu must be a pointer previously obtained from Net-SNMP and not already freed.
Do not use the pdu after calling snmp_free_pdu to avoid use-after-free.
Passing NULL may be accepted by some implementations, but this header does not guarantee NULL-safety; behavior on NULL is unspecified (inferred).

functions.name: snmp_pdu_add_variable
functions.signature: netsnmp_variable_list * snmp_pdu_add_variable(netsnmp_pdu *pdu, const oid *name, size_t name_length, u_char type, const void *value, size_t len);
functions.description: Adds a new variable binding to the given SNMP PDU. The varbind’s OID, ASN.1 type, and value are provided and attached to pdu. Returns a pointer to the created netsnmp_variable_list entry, or NULL on failure (exact error reporting not specified here). Typical usage: prepare a PDU, then call to append a varbind for GET/SET/GETNEXT requests.
requirements: pdu must point to a valid, initialized netsnmp_pdu.
name must point to a valid OID array of at least name_length elements; name_length is the number of sub-identifiers.
type must be a valid SNMP/ASN.1 type code recognized by Net-SNMP (e.g., ASN_INTEGER, ASN_OCTET_STR, etc.).

If value is non-NULL, it must point to at least len bytes of readable data appropriate for the given type; for types that carry no payload (e.g., ASN_NULL), len should typically be 0 and value may be ignored.
Function may allocate memory; caller must eventually free the resulting varbind(s) (e.g., via snmp_free_varbind on the PDU’s varbind list).
Do not modify or free the returned varbind through generic free routines other than the documented Net-SNMP APIs.

functions.name: snmp_varlist_add_variable
functions.signature: netsnmp_variable_list * snmp_varlist_add_variable(netsnmp_variable_list **varlist, const oid *name, size_t name_length, u_char type, const void *value, size_t len);
functions.description: Appends a new variable binding to the provided varlist head pointer, updating the list as needed. Creates a netsnmp_variable_list node with the given OID, type, and value. Returns a pointer to the created node, or NULL on failure (exact error reporting not specified).
requirements: varlist must be a valid pointer to a netsnmp_variable_list*; it may point to NULL to create the first element.
name must reference a valid OID array with at least name_length sub-identifiers.
type must be a valid SNMP/ASN.1 type code recognized by Net-SNMP.
If value is non-NULL, it must reference at least len bytes appropriate for type; for ASN_NULL-like types, len is typically 0.
On success, the function may update *varlist; callers must later free the resulting list with snmp_free_varbind.
Do not pass a corrupted or cyclic list pointer.

functions.name: snmp_add_null_var
functions.signature: netsnmp_variable_list * snmp_add_null_var(netsnmp_pdu *pdu, const oid *name, size_t name_length);
functions.description: Convenience helper that adds a varbind with a NULL value (ASN_NULL) to the specified PDU for the given OID. Commonly used for GET/GETNEXT/GETBULK where values are not supplied. Returns a pointer to the created varbind, or NULL on failure.
requirements: pdu must be a valid, initialized netsnmp_pdu.
name must be a valid OID array with at least name_length elements.
Adds a NULL-typed varbind; no value buffer is required.
Caller must free varbinds associated with the PDU using appropriate Net-SNMP free routines (e.g., snmp_free_varbind).

functions.name: snmp_clone_varbind
functions.description: Clones a variable binding or a chain of variable bindings. Returns a deep copy of the provided varbind (and subsequent list if varlist->next is set), or NULL on failure. Useful for duplicating varbinds across PDUs or saving snapshots.
requirements: varlist must point to a valid netsnmp_variable_list node (optionally the head of a list).
All data referenced by varlist must be in a consistent, initialized state so a deep copy can be made.
Caller takes ownership of the returned clone and must free it using snmp_free_varbind.
Do not pass an already-freed or partially-initialized varbind.

functions.name: snmp_set_var_objid
functions.signature: int snmp_set_var_objid(netsnmp_variable_list *var, const oid *name, size_t name_length);
functions.description: Sets the OID (object identifier) of an existing varbind to the provided OID. Returns an int status (exact semantics not specified here). Intended to update or initialize the name field of a netsnmp_variable_list entry.
requirements: var must be a valid, initialized netsnmp_variable_list pointer.
name must reference a valid OID array with at least name_length elements.
var’s previous OID, if any, will be replaced; subsequent operations should use the updated OID.
Caller should check the return value and handle failure per project conventions (exact values not documented here).

functions.name: snmp_set_var_value
functions.signature: int snmp_set_var_value(netsnmp_variable_list *var, const void *value, size_t len);
functions.description: Sets the raw value payload of an existing varbind (without changing its type). Returns an int status (exact semantics unspecified in this header). Use when the varbind type is already determined and you need to supply or update its data buffer.
requirements: var must be a valid, initialized netsnmp_variable_list with a coherent type already set.
If value is non-NULL, it must point to at least len bytes of readable memory; len specifies the payload length.
The provided data must be appropriate for var->type; mismatches may fail or produce undefined results (header does not specify).
Caller should check and handle the return code according to Net-SNMP conventions.

functions.name: snmp_set_var_typed_value
functions.signature: int snmp_set_var_typed_value(netsnmp_variable_list *var, u_char type, const void *value, size_t len);
functions.description: Sets both the ASN.1 type and the value of a varbind. Returns an int status (exact semantics not specified). Useful for initializing a varbind in one call.
requirements: var must be a valid, initialized netsnmp_variable_list.
type must be a valid Net-SNMP/ASN.1 type code compatible with the provided value.
If value is non-NULL, it must point to at least len bytes; for types that carry no payload (e.g., ASN_NULL), len is typically 0.
Caller should verify the return status and handle errors appropriately.

functions.name: snmp_set_var_typed_integer
functions.description: Sets the varbind to an integer-like ASN.1 type and assigns the provided long value. Returns an int status (exact semantics not specified). Intended for setting INTEGER, GAUGE, COUNTER, TIME_TICKS, or similar integer-based types as supported by Net-SNMP.
requirements: var must be a valid, initialized netsnmp_variable_list.
type must be an ASN.1 integer-compatible type supported by Net-SNMP (e.g., ASN_INTEGER or similar).
Value val must be within the representable range of the specified ASN.1 type; overflow/underflow behavior is not described here.
Caller should check the return code to detect failures.

functions.name: print_variable
functions.signature: void print_variable(const oid *objid, size_t objidlen, const netsnmp_variable_list *variable);
functions.description: Prints a human-readable representation of the given OID and associated varbind value to the default output (typically stdout). Intended for debugging or CLI-style output. No return value.
requirements: objid must reference a valid OID array of at least objidlen elements.
variable must point to a valid, initialized netsnmp_variable_list corresponding to objid.
Output destination is implementation-defined (likely stdout); ensure the environment allows writing to standard output.

functions.name: fprint_variable
functions.signature: void fprint_variable(FILE *fp, const oid *objid, size_t objidlen, const netsnmp_variable_list *variable);
functions.description: Prints a human-readable representation of the given OID and varbind value to the provided FILE stream.
requirements: fp must be a valid FILE* opened for writing.
objid must reference a valid OID array with at least objidlen elements.
variable must point to a valid, initialized netsnmp_variable_list.

functions.name: snprint_variable
functions.signature: int snprint_variable(char *buf, size_t buf_len, const oid *objid, size_t objidlen, const netsnmp_variable_list *variable);
functions.description: Formats a human-readable representation of the OID and varbind value into the provided character buffer. Returns an int (typical Net-SNMP semantics are number of characters written or -1 on error, but exact behavior is not specified in this header).
requirements: buf must point to a writable buffer of at least buf_len bytes.
buf_len must accurately reflect the buffer size to avoid overflow.
objid must reference a valid OID array of at least objidlen elements.
variable must be a valid, initialized netsnmp_variable_list.

functions.name: print_value
functions.signature: void print_value(const oid *objid, size_t objidlen, const netsnmp_variable_list *variable);
functions.description: Prints only the value part of a varbind (without the OID) to the default output (typically stdout). Useful when the OID context is already known. No return value.
requirements: objid must reference a valid OID array with at least objidlen elements (used to interpret/format the value).
variable must point to a valid, initialized netsnmp_variable_list.
Environment must allow writing to standard output.

functions.name: fprint_value
functions.signature: void fprint_value(FILE *fp, const oid *objid, size_t objidlen, const netsnmp_variable_list *variable);
functions.description: Prints only the varbind’s value (no OID) to the specified FILE stream.
requirements: fp must be a valid FILE* opened for writing.
objid must reference a valid OID array with at least objidlen elements.
variable must be a valid, initialized netsnmp_variable_list.

functions.name: snprint_value
functions.signature: int snprint_value(char *buf, size_t buf_len, const oid *objid, size_t objidlen, const netsnmp_variable_list *variable);
functions.description: Formats only the value portion of a varbind into the provided buffer. Returns an int (commonly number of characters written or -1 on error in Net-SNMP, but exact semantics are not specified here).
requirements: buf must be a writable buffer of at least buf_len bytes.
buf_len must be the actual capacity of buf to prevent overflow.
objid must reference a valid OID array with at least objidlen elements (may guide formatting).
variable must be a valid, initialized netsnmp_variable_list.

functions.name: snmp_free_var
functions.description: Frees a single netsnmp_variable_list node and its associated resources. Does not free subsequent nodes. Use to release an individual varbind.
requirements: var must either be NULL or point to a varbind previously allocated by Net-SNMP APIs; passing arbitrary or stack-allocated objects leads to undefined behavior.
If var is part of a list, unlink it before freeing to avoid corrupting the list.
Do not access var after this call (use-after-free).
Do not double-free the same varbind.

functions.name: snmp_free_varbind
functions.description: Frees an entire linked list of netsnmp_variable_list nodes starting at varlist. Use to release all varbinds in a list or those attached to a PDU.
requirements: varlist may be NULL; otherwise it must be a list allocated/managed by Net-SNMP varbind creation APIs.
After freeing, all nodes in the list become invalid; do not access them.
Do not double-free; call at most once for a given list head.
If the list is still attached to a PDU or external structure, detach references before freeing to avoid dangling pointers.

functions.name: add_mibdir
functions.description: Adds a directory to the Net-SNMP MIB search path so that subsequent MIB loads can find files in that directory. Typically called before reading or initializing MIBs.
requirements: The argument must point to a valid, null-terminated directory path string.
Call before functions that load/read MIBs (e.g., netsnmp_init_mib, read_mib, read_all_mibs) to affect their search path.
The directory must be accessible/readable by the process.

functions.name: netsnmp_init_mib
functions.description: Initializes the MIB subsystem. Sets up internal structures and loads configured/standard MIBs so that name-to-OID and OID-to-name lookups can work.
requirements: Should be called once early in program startup before using MIB-dependent APIs (e.g., read_objid by name, get_module_node, print_description).
Must not be called concurrently from multiple threads without external synchronization (thread-safety of initialization is unknown).

functions.name: init_mib
functions.description: Legacy alias for netsnmp_init_mib(). Initializes the MIB subsystem. Provided for backward compatibility.
requirements: Same requirements as netsnmp_init_mib.
Prefer netsnmp_init_mib in new code.

functions.name: init_mib_internals
functions.description: Initializes internal MIB processing structures without performing full external MIB loading. Typically used by library internals; legacy/compatibility entry point.
requirements: Intended for internal/advanced usage; exact effects beyond internal setup are unknown.
Do not rely on this alone for full MIB name lookups unless you know the internals.

functions.name: shutdown_mib
functions.description: Shuts down and cleans up the MIB subsystem, releasing resources allocated during initialization and MIB loading.
requirements: Should be called once during program shutdown, after all MIB-dependent operations have completed.
Do not use MIB-dependent APIs after calling this function.

functions.name: netsnmp_read_module
functions.description: Loads/parses the specified MIB module by name and returns the root of its parsed tree representation.
requirements: The argument must be a valid, null-terminated module name string (not a file path).
netsnmp_init_mib (or equivalent MIB setup) should be performed before calling to ensure search paths and tokens are configured.
Return value must be checked for NULL to detect errors.

functions.name: read_module
functions.description: Legacy alias for netsnmp_read_module(). Loads/parses the specified MIB module by name and returns its tree root.
requirements: Same requirements as netsnmp_read_module.
Return value must be checked for NULL to detect errors.

functions.name: read_mib
functions.description: Parses a MIB from the specified file (path) and returns the tree structure for the parsed content. Used to explicitly load a particular MIB file.
requirements: Argument must be a valid, null-terminated path to a readable MIB file.
Caller should check the return value for NULL to detect parse/load errors.
Call after configuring search paths (e.g., add_mibdir) if using relative paths.

functions.name: read_all_mibs
functions.description: Loads/parses all MIBs found along the configured search path and returns the resulting (global) MIB tree root.
requirements: Should be called after search paths are set (e.g., add_mibdir) and after initialization (netsnmp_init_mib) if required by your setup.
May be expensive; avoid in performance-sensitive paths.
Return value should be checked for NULL on failure.

functions.name: add_module_replacement
functions.signature: void add_module_replacement(const char *, const char *, const char *, int);
functions.description: Registers a module replacement rule to map one MIB module name to another (optionally conditioned by context/version), aiding migration and compatibility when module names change.
requirements: All string arguments must be valid, null-terminated strings (semantics of the third string and the integer flag are library-defined; exact meanings are unknown here).
Call before loading/reading modules so replacement can take effect.

functions.name: snmp_set_mib_warnings
functions.description: Controls the verbosity/level of MIB warning messages emitted during MIB parsing and processing.
requirements: Argument must be an integer level; valid range/values are library-defined (unknown here).
Call before or during MIB parsing to affect subsequent diagnostics.

functions.name: snmp_set_mib_errors
functions.description: Enables or configures the reporting of MIB parsing errors.
requirements: Argument must be an integer level/flag; exact accepted values are library-defined (unknown here).
Call before or during MIB parsing to affect error reporting.

functions.name: snmp_set_save_descriptions
functions.description: Toggles whether textual descriptions from MIBs are saved/retained in memory for later retrieval/printing.
requirements: Argument is treated as boolean/flag (nonzero to enable, zero to disable; precise interpretation is library-defined).
Set before loading MIBs to ensure descriptions are captured.

functions.name: read_objid
functions.description: Parses an OID given as a string (numeric dotted or MIB name form) into an array of oid sub-identifiers. Writes the parsed OID into the provided buffer and sets the resulting length.
requirements: First argument must be a valid, null-terminated OID string (e.g., ".1.3.6.1..." or "iso.org.dod..." or "mibName::object").
Second argument (oid array) must point to a writable buffer large enough to hold the parsed sub-identifiers.
Third argument points to a size_t that on input contains the capacity of the oid buffer in number of sub-identifiers; on output it is set to the number written.
Caller must initialize *size_t to the buffer capacity before calling.
Returns nonzero on success and 0 on failure (conventional for this API; exact return convention should be checked in the library).
MIBs must be initialized/loaded to resolve non-numeric names.

functions.name: snmp_parse_oid
functions.description: Parses an OID string into an array of oid sub-identifiers, returning a pointer to the resulting array (typically the provided buffer) or NULL on error.
requirements: OID string must be valid and null-terminated.
If a buffer (second arg) is provided, it must be writable and large enough for the parsed OID; the size pointer must indicate its capacity on input and receives the parsed length on output.
The function may return NULL on parse/lookup failure; caller must check the return value.
Behavior when the buffer is NULL is library-defined and unknown here; do not pass NULL unless you know the library contracts.
MIBs must be initialized/loaded to resolve non-numeric names.

functions.name: get_module_node
functions.signature: int get_module_node(const char *, const char *, oid *, size_t *);
functions.description: Finds an OID node by its name within a specific MIB module and returns its numeric OID in the provided buffer.
requirements: First argument must be an object/node name string; second is a module name string; both must be valid, null-terminated strings.
The oid buffer must be writable and large enough; the size pointer must be set to the buffer capacity (in sub-identifiers) on input and receives the resulting length.
Return value must be checked to detect failure (nonzero/zero semantics are library-defined; unknown here).
MIBs must be loaded/initialized so the module and node can be resolved.

functions.name: print_mib
functions.description: Prints the currently loaded MIB tree to the given FILE stream in a human-readable format (for diagnostics/debugging).
requirements: FILE* must be a valid, open output stream.
MIBs should be initialized/loaded for meaningful output.

functions.name: print_objid
functions.description: Prints a human-readable representation of the given OID to the default output (typically stdout).
requirements: The oid pointer must reference a valid array of at least the specified number of sub-identifiers.
The length argument is the number of sub-identifiers in the OID and must be accurate and nonzero for non-empty OIDs.
MIBs should be loaded to print in symbolic form; otherwise numeric form may be printed.

functions.name: fprint_objid
functions.description: Prints a human-readable representation of the given OID to the specified FILE stream.
requirements: FILE* must be a valid, open output stream.
The oid pointer must reference a valid array of at least the specified number of sub-identifiers.
Length must match the number of sub-identifiers in the OID and be non-negative (size_t).
MIBs should be loaded to print in symbolic form; otherwise numeric form may be printed.

functions.name: snprint_objid
functions.signature: int snprint_objid(char *, size_t, const oid *, size_t);
functions.description: Formats the given OID into a human-readable string in the caller-provided buffer, returning the number of characters written or a negative value on error.
requirements: Buffer pointer must be non-NULL when buf_len > 0; buf_len specifies the size in bytes and should include space for the terminating null.
The oid pointer must reference a valid array of length objidlen (number of sub-identifiers).
Caller must check the return value to detect truncation or errors (exact convention is library-defined; unknown here).
MIBs should be loaded to get symbolic names; otherwise numeric form may be used.

functions.name: print_description
functions.description: Prints the textual description for the specified OID to the default output, wrapping to the specified width. The OID identifies the MIB node whose DESCRIPTION is printed.
requirements: The oid pointer must reference a valid OID array of the given length.
Width should be a positive integer to enable proper wrapping; behavior for non-positive width is library-defined (unknown).
MIBs must be loaded with saved descriptions (snmp_set_save_descriptions enabled before loading) to have descriptions available.

functions.name: fprint_description
functions.description: Prints the textual description for the specified OID to the given FILE stream, wrapping to the specified width.
requirements: FILE* must be a valid, open output stream.
The oid pointer must reference a valid OID array of the given length.
Width should be a positive integer; behavior otherwise is unknown.
MIBs must be loaded with descriptions saved to retrieve and print them.

functions.name: snprint_description
functions.signature: int snprint_description(char *, size_t, oid *, size_t, int);
functions.description: Formats the textual description for the specified OID into the caller-provided buffer, wrapping to the specified width. Returns the number of characters written or a negative value on error.
requirements: Buffer pointer must be non-NULL when buf_len > 0; buf_len is the total buffer size in bytes and should include space for the terminating null.
The oid pointer must reference a valid OID array of length objidlen (number of sub-identifiers).
Width should be a positive integer; behavior otherwise is unknown.
MIBs must be loaded with descriptions saved (enable before loading) to produce description text.
Caller must check the return value to detect truncation or errors (exact convention is library-defined; unknown).

functions.name: register_config_handler
functions.signature: struct config_line *register_config_handler(const char *filePrefix, const char *token, void (*parser)(const char *, char *), void (*releaser)(void), const char *usageLine);
functions.description: Registers a configuration directive handler for the given file prefix and token. When configuration files are read, lines starting with the specified token (within files matching the filePrefix) will be dispatched to the provided parser callback. The releaser callback (if used) is intended to free any resources allocated by the handler during parsing. usageLine is a help/usage string for diagnostics. Typical usage is to call this during application/library initialization, before reading configuration files.
requirements: filePrefix must point to a valid, null-terminated string identifying which config file set this handler applies to (exact matching rules are not specified in this header).
token must point to a valid, null-terminated string naming the configuration directive to handle.
parser must be a valid function pointer matching void(const char *token, char *line) and must tolerate being called with the token for the directive and the remainder of the line to parse.
releaser, if supplied by the caller, must be a valid function pointer taking no arguments and safe to call when configuration state is being torn down (exact call timing unspecified).
usageLine, if supplied, should be a valid, null-terminated help string describing the syntax of the token (exact formatting unspecified).
To affect configuration parsing, this function should be called before read_configs().
Thread-safety and reentrancy of the callbacks are unknown and not specified in this header.

functions.name: register_const_config_handler
functions.signature: struct config_line *register_const_config_handler(const char *filePrefix, const char *token, void (*parser)(const char *, const char *), void (*releaser)(void), const char *usageLine);
functions.description: Registers a configuration directive handler whose parser receives the remaining line as a const char*. This is used when the parser does not need to modify the input buffer. Behavior is otherwise analogous to register_config_handler.
requirements: filePrefix must be a valid, null-terminated string identifying the target config file set.
token must be a valid, null-terminated directive name.
parser must be a valid function pointer matching void(const char *token, const char *line) and should not attempt to modify the line buffer.
releaser, if provided, must be a valid no-arg function used to free any resources allocated by the handler.
usageLine, if provided, should be a valid help string.
To be effective for the current run, register before read_configs().
Other lifecycle, threading, and error semantics are not specified here (unknown).

functions.name: register_prenetsnmp_mib_handler
functions.signature: struct config_line *register_prenetsnmp_mib_handler(const char *filePrefix, const char *token, void (*parser)(const char *, char *), void (*releaser)(void), const char *usageLine);
functions.description: Registers a configuration handler intended to run during the pre-MIB configuration phase. Handlers registered here are used when reading "pre-MIB" configuration files or phases (prior to full MIB initialization). Usage mirrors register_config_handler but for the earlier phase.
requirements: filePrefix must be a valid, null-terminated identifier for the applicable pre-MIB config files.
token must be a valid, null-terminated directive name.
parser must be a valid function pointer matching void(const char *token, char *line).
releaser, if provided, must be a valid no-arg function for cleanup associated with this handler.
usageLine, if provided, should be a valid help string.
Register before calling read_premib_configs() for the handler to be used in the pre-MIB phase.
Exact error return conditions and threading guarantees are not documented here (unknown).

functions.name: unregister_config_handler
functions.description: Removes a previously registered configuration handler for the specified filePrefix and token. After unregistering, matching directives will no longer be dispatched to that handler.
requirements: filePrefix must be the same identifier used during registration (valid, null-terminated string).
token must be the same directive name used during registration (valid, null-terminated string).
Should be called after a corresponding register_*_handler; behavior when no matching handler exists is not specified (unknown).
Do not call during active parsing unless the library explicitly supports it (support not specified here; unknown).

functions.name: register_mib_handlers
functions.description: Registers built-in MIB-related configuration handlers. Defined in mib.c, it prepares the library’s default MIB handler set before configuration parsing or agent initialization.
requirements: Call during initialization before reading configuration, if the application relies on built-in MIB handlers.
No arguments; may be a no-op if already registered (idempotency not specified; unknown).

functions.name: unregister_all_config_handlers
functions.description: Unregisters all configuration handlers that have been registered. Typically used during shutdown or reinitialization to clear handler state.
requirements: Intended to be called when no configuration parsing is in progress (concurrency semantics not specified; unknown).
After calling, previously registered handlers will no longer be invoked until re-registered.
Effect on handlers’ releaser callbacks (whether they are called) is not specified here (unknown).

functions.name: register_app_config_handler
functions.signature: struct config_line *register_app_config_handler(const char *token, void (*parser)(const char *, char *), void (*releaser)(void), const char *usageLine);
functions.description: Registers an application-specific configuration handler that is not tied to a particular file prefix. The handler will be invoked for the given token when application configuration directives are parsed.
requirements: token must be a valid, null-terminated directive name.
parser must be a valid function pointer matching void(const char *token, char *line).
releaser, if provided, must be a valid no-arg function for cleanup when configuration is reset or unloaded.
usageLine, if provided, should be a valid help string for usage output.
Register before read_configs() so that directives are recognized.
Exact file scope and matching rules for application handlers are not specified here (unknown).

functions.name: register_app_prenetsnmp_mib_handler
functions.signature: struct config_line *register_app_prenetsnmp_mib_handler(const char *token, void (*parser)(const char *, char *), void (*releaser)(void), const char *usageLine);
functions.description: Registers an application-specific configuration handler for the pre-NET-SNMP-MIB phase. Similar to register_app_config_handler, but intended to be used during read_premib_configs().
requirements: token must be a valid, null-terminated directive name.
parser must be a valid function pointer matching void(const char *token, char *line).
releaser, if provided, must be a valid no-arg function for cleanup.
usageLine, if provided, should be a valid help string.
Register before calling read_premib_configs() to have effect in the pre-MIB phase.

functions.name: unregister_app_config_handler
functions.description: Unregisters an application-specific configuration handler previously registered for the given token. After this call, the token will no longer be dispatched to the app handler.
requirements: token must be the same directive name used during registration (valid, null-terminated string).
Should be called after a corresponding register_app_*_handler; behavior when no handler is registered is not specified (unknown).
Avoid calling during active parsing unless the library documents support for it (unknown here).

functions.name: read_configs
functions.description: Parses and loads standard Net-SNMP configuration files into the library’s internal state. Registered handlers will be invoked for recognized directives during this process.
requirements: Call after registering any needed handlers via register_* functions so they are active during parsing.
May read from default configuration locations as defined by the library; exact search order and environment influences are not specified here (unknown).
Should be called once during initialization unless repeated reload is explicitly supported (not specified here; unknown).

functions.name: read_premib_configs
functions.description: Parses and loads pre-MIB configuration files/sections. Handlers registered via pre-MIB registration functions will be invoked during this phase, typically before full MIB initialization.
requirements: Call before read_configs() when a two-phase configuration is expected and pre-MIB settings are needed.
Ensure any required pre-MIB handlers are registered beforehand.
Exact file set and ordering are not specified here (unknown).

functions.name: read_config_print_usage
functions.description: Prints usage/help information for registered configuration tokens, optionally prefixed by the given lead string. Useful for generating command-line or documentation help output.
requirements: lead should be a valid, null-terminated string to prefix usage lines (whether NULL is allowed is not specified; unknown).
Should be called after registering handlers so their usage lines are available.

functions.name: config_perror
functions.description: Reports a configuration error message associated with the most recent parsing context. Typically used within parser callbacks to emit an error for an invalid directive or argument.
requirements: Argument must be a valid, null-terminated error message string (whether NULL is permitted to reference a stored error is not specified; unknown).
Call within or after configuration parsing where a parsing context exists; behavior outside that context is not specified (unknown).

functions.name: config_pwarn
functions.description: Reports a configuration warning message associated with the current or most recent parsing context. Typically used by parser callbacks for non-fatal issues.
requirements: Argument must be a valid, null-terminated warning message string (NULL allowance not specified; unknown).
Intended for use during configuration parsing; behavior outside that context is not specified (unknown).

functions.name: snmp_error
functions.description: Retrieves the most recent error status/details for an SNMP session. Intended to be called after a library call fails to obtain a C library errno (if any), an SNMP-specific error code, and a human-readable error string for diagnostics.
requirements: sess should point to a valid, initialized netsnmp_session associated with the failed operation.
clib_errorno may be NULL; if non-NULL, it will be set to a C library error number (errno) or 0.
snmp_errorno may be NULL; if non-NULL, it will be set to a Net-SNMP library/protocol error code.
errstring may be NULL; if non-NULL and an error message exists, it will be set to a dynamically allocated string; the caller must free it with free() when done.
Call only after a library operation sets an error on the session; values are otherwise implementation-defined.

functions.name: snmp_sess_error
functions.signature: void snmp_sess_error(struct session_list *slp, int *clib_errorno, int *snmp_errorno, char **errstring);
functions.description: Retrieves the most recent error status/details for an internal session_list handle (single-session API). Used by lower-level/session-iterator code to query errors without a public netsnmp_session pointer.
requirements: slp must refer to a valid struct session_list for an active/known session.
clib_errorno/snmp_errorno may be NULL; if non-NULL, they are set to the respective error codes.
errstring may be NULL; if non-NULL and an error message exists, it will be set to a dynamically allocated string; the caller must free it with free().
Call only after an operation on the session_list has failed; otherwise results are implementation-defined.

functions.name: snmp_api_errstring
functions.description: Returns a static human-readable description for a Net-SNMP library (API) error code (not protocol error). Useful for turning error codes from snmp_error into messages.
requirements: snmp_errorno should be a valid Net-SNMP API error code; passing unknown values yields an implementation-defined string (often "Unknown error").
Returned pointer refers to static storage; do not free or modify.

functions.name: snmp_errstring
functions.description: Returns a static human-readable description for an SNMP protocol error/status code. Typically used for PDU error-status values or protocol-level errors.
requirements: snmp_errorno should be a valid SNMP protocol error/status code.
Returned pointer refers to static storage; do not free or modify.

functions.name: snmp_perror
functions.description: Prints a formatted parsing-related error message to the logging facility (historically stderr or configured logs), prefixed by msg. Intended for MIB/config parsing errors.
requirements: msg may be NULL or a C string; if provided, it should be a valid NUL-terminated string.
Relies on the library’s current logging configuration; ensure logging is enabled if you expect output.

functions.name: snmp_sess_perror
functions.description: Logs a descriptive message for the last error associated with sess, prefixed by msg. Use for general Net-SNMP library errors tied to a session.
requirements: sess must point to a valid, initialized netsnmp_session that has experienced an error.
msg may be NULL or a valid NUL-terminated string to prefix the message.
Relies on the library’s logging configuration; ensure logging is enabled for output.

functions.name: snmp_log_perror
functions.description: Logs a system (C library) error message, similar to perror(msg), through the Net-SNMP logging facility. Useful for reporting errno-based failures in a consistent way.
requirements: msg may be NULL or a valid NUL-terminated string.
Assumes errno is set appropriately at the time of the call.
Output destination depends on current Net-SNMP logging configuration.

functions.name: snmp_log
functions.signature: int snmp_log(int priority, const char *format, ...) NETSNMP_ATTRIBUTE_FORMAT(printf, 2, 3);
functions.description: Logs a message to the Net-SNMP logging subsystem with the given priority using printf-style formatting. Use this to write application/library logs via Net-SNMP’s configured outputs (file, syslog, etc.).
requirements: priority should be a valid logging priority value compatible with the library’s logging backend (typically syslog priorities like LOG_ERR/LOG_INFO).
format must be a valid NUL-terminated printf-style format string.
Variadic arguments must match the format specifiers exactly; the function is annotated for compile-time format checking.
Returns an int status (implementation-defined: commonly number of bytes written or a negative value on error); callers should check the return value for errors.
Thread-safety depends on the library build/configuration; avoid mixing with shutdown/restart logging calls concurrently.

functions.name: snmp_vlog
functions.signature: int snmp_vlog(int priority, const char *format, va_list ap);
functions.description: va_list variant of snmp_log. Logs a formatted message with the specified priority using a provided va_list.

functions.name: snmp_disable_log

requirements: Call during orderly shutdown when no other threads are emitting logs.

functions.name: debug_disable_token_logs

Call early in program initialization or prior to emitting debug messages for predictable behavior.

functions.name: snmp_get_do_debugging

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets a generic null-terminated C string expected by many
# Net-SNMP APIs in the provided fuzz stubs. We craft a single buffer that
# concatenates multiple plausible C-strings separated by NULs so the harness
# can carve them as needed for FUZZ_PARAM_STR and similar calls.
#
# Strategy:
# - Produce a collection of directory-like paths, module/token names, and
#   human-readable text lines. Include edge cases (root "/", empty component,
#   Windows-style backslashes) and typical valid forms.
# - Keep everything valid and NUL-terminated. The overall buffer is a sequence
#   of independent C-strings separated by NUL. No trailing garbage beyond the
#   final NULs.
# - Limit total size to <= 4096 bytes.

SAFE_ASCII = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_+."

MODULE_PREFIXES = [
    "SNMPv2-MIB", "IF-MIB", "IP-MIB", "TCP-MIB", "UDP-MIB", "HOST-RESOURCES-MIB",
    "UCD-SNMP-MIB", "NET-SNMP-AGENT-MIB", "DISMAN-EVENT-MIB", "BRIDGE-MIB",
]

TOKENS = [
    "com2sec", "rwcommunity", "rocommunity", "view", "access", "rouser",
    "sysLocation", "sysContact", "trap2sink", "agentAddress", "proc",
]

# Some directory candidates (will be combined with mutations below)
DIR_BASES = ["/", ".", "..", "/usr/share/snmp/mibs", "/etc/snmp", "/tmp", "/var/tmp"]

def _rand(r: random.Random, seq: List[str]) -> str:
    return seq[r.randrange(len(seq))]

def rand_token(r: random.Random) -> str:
    base = _rand(r, TOKENS + MODULE_PREFIXES)
    # add optional suffix/prefix to diversify while keeping it valid
    decorations = ["", "_v3", "-alpha", "-beta", "_test", str(r.randrange(100))]
    part = base + _rand(r, decorations)
    # ensure only safe ascii
    return ''.join(ch for ch in part if ch in SAFE_ASCII)

def rand_module(r: random.Random) -> str:
    base = _rand(r, MODULE_PREFIXES)
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        base += "-EXT"
    return base

def rand_dir(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # generate Unix or Windows-like dirs, including edge cases
    style = r.randrange(3)
    if style == 0:
        # Unix absolute
        parts = [""]  # leading slash
        depth = r.randrange(0, 4)
        for _ in range(depth):
            # include empty segments sparsely to allow "/" and root-only
            if r.random() < 0.2:
                parts.append("")
            else:
                name = ''.join(r.choice(SAFE_ASCII) for _ in range(r.randrange(1, 8)))
                parts.append(name)
        return "/".join(parts) or "/"
    elif style == 1:
        # relative with dot segments
        base = _rand(r, [".", "..", "./mibs", "../mibs"])
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            tail = ''.join(r.choice(SAFE_ASCII) for _ in range(r.randrange(1, 8)))
            return base + "/" + tail
        return base
    else:
        # Windows-like
        drive = chr(r.randrange(ord('C'), ord('H'))) + ":\\"
        depth = r.randrange(0, 3)
        parts = []
        for _ in range(depth):
            name = ''.join(r.choice(SAFE_ASCII) for _ in range(r.randrange(1, 8)))
            parts.append(name)
        return drive + "\\".join(parts)

def rand_text(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Reasonable log/usage strings; keep under 256
    samples = [
        "usage: snmpapp -v3 -l authPriv -u user", 
        "error: invalid community string", 
        "warning: mib file not found", 
        "note: debug token enabled", 
        "trap sink configured",
    ]
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        return _rand(r, samples)
    # construct arbitrary but readable string
    words = [rand_token(r) for _ in range(r.randrange(3, 8))]
    return " ".join(words)[:256]

def rand_ctx(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # context strings for add_module_replacement
    options = ["", "any", "default", "snmpv2", "snmpv3", "agent", "subagent"]
    return _rand(r, options)

def _make_strings(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    out: List[str] = []
    # Ensure we have at least a good directory for add_mibdir success path
    # We include common existing dirs; harness may still check accessibility,
    # but these are typical locations.
    out.append(".")
    out.append("/")
    out.extend({rand_dir(r) for _ in range(6)})

    # Module replacements: old/new/ctx
    for _ in range(4):
        out.append(rand_module(r))
        out.append(rand_module(r))
        out.append(rand_ctx(r))

    # Tokens and usage lines for register_* handlers
    for _ in range(6):
        out.append(rand_token(r))
        out.append(rand_text(r))

    # Keys for snmp_sess_lookup_by_name
    for _ in range(4):
        out.append(rand_token(r))

    # Lead/prefix strings for usage and logging
    for _ in range(5):
        out.append(rand_text(r))

    # Cap length and ensure uniqueness sparsely while keeping order reasonable
    # Keep strings non-empty; replace empties with "."
    cleaned = []
    for s in out:
        if not s:
            s = "."
        if len(s) > 256:
            s = s[:256]
        cleaned.append(s)
    return cleaned

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    strings = _make_strings(r)

    # Shuffle to mix categories and improve coverage across calls consuming FUZZ_PARAM_STR
    r.shuffle(strings)

    # Build a NUL-separated blob of C-strings, and also ensure final string is NUL-terminated
    blob_parts: List[bytes] = []
    total = 0
    for s in strings:
        b = s.encode('utf-8') + b"\x00"
        if total + len(b) > 4096:
            break
        blob_parts.append(b)
        total += len(b)

    # Guarantee at least one terminator
    if not blob_parts:
        blob_parts.append(b".\x00")

    return b"".join(blob_parts)

import os
import random
from typing import List

def _rand_bytes(r: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))

def _make_integer_payload(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Net-SNMP stubs pass a long by value pointer; produce 8 bytes to be broadly compatible
    # even though the fuzzer stub will treat buffer opaquely when used for OCTET STRING too.
    # Encode signed 64-bit in native-endian like content; consumers interpret as raw bytes.
    val = r.randint(-2**63, 2**63 - 1)
    return val.to_bytes(8, byteorder='little', signed=True)

def _make_octet_string_payload(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Construct interesting OCTET STRINGs: mix of ASCII, UTF-8, binary, and lengths near edges
    choices: List[bytes] = []
    # ASCII words
    words = [b"public", b"private", b"publicpublic", b"authPriv", b"context", b"engineID"]
    choices.extend(words)
    # UTF-8 sequences
    choices.extend([
        "こんにちは".encode("utf-8"),
        "пароль".encode("utf-8"),
        "παράδειγμα".encode("utf-8"),
    ])
    # Binary patterns
    choices.extend([
        b"\x00" * 0,
        b"\x00",
        b"\x00" * 8,
        b"\xff" * 8,
        bytes(range(1, 16)),
        os.urandom(16),
    ])
    # Length-biased random
    lens = [0, 1, 2, 3, 7, 8, 15, 16, 31, 32, 63, 64, 127, 128, 255, 256, 511]
    L = r.choice(lens)
    if L > 0:
        choices.append(_rand_bytes(r, L))
    s = r.choice(choices)
    # Limit overall size elsewhere; return as is (<= 512 is desired by stubs)
    return s[:512]

def _make_object_identifier_payload(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # OBJECT IDENTIFIER value buffer in stubs is an array of oid sub-identifiers (unsigned long).
    # We will emit as raw bytes; the fuzzer runtime provides OID arrays internally. For our
    # arbitrary buffer, craft something that could be interpreted as such: sequence of 32-bit.
    length_subids = r.randint(1, 16)
    subids = [r.randrange(0, 2**31) for _ in range(length_subids)]
    b = bytearray()
    for s in subids:
        b += s.to_bytes(4, byteorder='little', signed=False)
    return bytes(b)

def _compose_cases(r: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    cases: List[bytes] = []
    # Case A: INTEGER-like payload
    cases.append(_make_integer_payload(r))
    # Case B: OCTET STRING with typical SNMP community/value strings
    cases.append(_make_octet_string_payload(r))
    # Case C: NULL-like (empty)
    cases.append(b"")
    # Case D: OBJECT IDENTIFIER-like payload
    cases.append(_make_object_identifier_payload(r))
    # Case E: Mixed: OID-ish followed by octet string
    mix = _make_object_identifier_payload(r) + _make_octet_string_payload(r)
    cases.append(mix[:512])
    # Case F: Boundary size near 512 used by stubs
    boundary = _rand_bytes(r, 512)
    cases.append(boundary)
    return cases

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    cases = _compose_cases(r)
    buf = r.choice(cases)
    # Ensure final buffer size is within 4096 (and within stub expectations ~512 for values)
    if len(buf) > 4096:
        buf = buf[:4096]
    return bytes(buf)

# This generator produces paths and file contents suitable for the provided fuzzer stubs.
# Stubs use FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME() to obtain a temporary file path and then write to it.

def _rand_ident(rng: random.Random, min_len=3, max_len=10) -> str:
    first = rng.choice(string.ascii_uppercase)
    rest = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + '-') for _ in range(rng.randint(min_len-1, max_len-1)))
    # Hyphen not allowed at end in many parsers; ensure last is alnum
    if not rest or not rest[-1].isalnum():
        rest = (rest[:-1] if rest else '') + rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits)
    return first + rest


def _build_mib(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    name = _rand_ident(rng)
    ent = rng.randint(1000, 999999)
    prefix = _rand_ident(rng)
    tmpl = rng.choice(MODULE_TEMPLATES)
    mib = tmpl.format(name=name, prefix=prefix, ent=ent)
    # Add optional comments and whitespace to exercise parser
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        comment_lines = ["-- " + ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + ' ') for _ in range(rng.randint(5, 40))) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3))]
        mib = '\n'.join(comment_lines) + '\n' + mib
    return mib.encode('ascii')


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose among: valid MIBs of varying complexity, or plain content for print_* stubs
    mode = rng.random()
    if mode < 0.85:
        data = _build_mib(rng)
    else:
        # For print_* stubs, any writable file is sufficient; include some OID/value text
        lines = []
        for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 12)):
            if rng.random() < 0.5:
                # OID dotted numeric
                oid = '.' + '.'.join(str(rng.randint(0, 4294967295)) for _ in range(rng.randint(5, 12)))
                lines.append(oid)

                s = ''.join(rng.choice(string.printable[:-6]) for _ in range(rng.randint(10, 60)))
                lines.append(s)
        data = ('\n'.join(lines) + '\n').encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
